A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FLy research. The main text, equations, ten tables, four figures, and Appendices A-F are readable and can be matched across pagination changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original FLy speedup, accuracy, timing, and accepted-token measurements, including component ablations, cross-model comparisons, and appendix batch-size experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results. Its clarification that JudgeDecoding scores come from another paper does not change the presence of original FLy experiments.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A retain the entropy gate, deferred window, boundary rejection rule, and prompt-lookup-based multi-level acceleration. The added explanation of acceleration does not modify the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ACP-prog-gen, NIAH-multivalue, MGSM in German/French/Thai, GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP. The appendices retain the same batch-size experiments and GSM8K case study; verbatim reproduction is discussed only as a limitation.

E2.justification: Tables 2-3 retain EAGLE-2, EAGLE-3, speculative sampling, REST, and TokenRecycling in their corresponding comparisons; Figure 3 retains JudgeDecoding. Newly discussed related-work methods are not added to the evaluations.

E3.justification: The model pairings, metrics, temperatures, W=6, entropy threshold 0.3, and draft lengths 15/25 remain unchanged. HumanEval ablation settings and Appendix D batch sizes 2/4/8/16 are also retained.

E4.justification: Section 3.4 and Appendices C-E retain the same hyperparameter, acceleration, drafter-size, cross-model, batch-size, and case-study analyses. The added distribution-shift paragraph discusses existing comparisons without introducing a new test.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point-estimate practice, without seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative case study are unchanged. Section 3.2 newly quotes EAGLE-3's ID/OOD speedups of 3.83x/1.56x and FLy's 2.63x/2.53x, but these already appear in Tables 2-3 at temperature 0 in v1.

T1.justification: Equations 1-12 retain the same mathematical definitions and acceptance rules. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of training-free semantic verification, model-agnostic acceleration, at least 99% accuracy recovery, and OOD robustness. The headline speedup claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 5 explicitly identifies verbatim passage or poem reproduction as an applicability limitation and consolidates the previously acknowledged performance gap to trained methods. Section 2.3 additionally clarifies that multi-level acceleration is orthogonal to verification.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract. Section 3.3 newly discloses that JudgeDecoding scores were taken from its original paper because its implementation was not open-sourced. FLy's implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds citations and discussion of GLIDE, HASS, speculative sampling by Chen et al., Draft&Verify, SWIFT, and KNN-SSD. It also reclassifies the existing LayerSkip reference as training-based and explains its training requirement. The overall taxonomy and FLy's principal positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized explanatory additions, expands related work, inserts a limitations section before the conclusion, and adjusts terminology and author-footnote wording. Most prose and the complete appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V3 adds conference headers and adjusts spacing and placement: Figure 3 moves from page 7 to page 8, and Tables 5-6 move from page 8 to page 9. Figure designs, legends, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 improves transparency by explicitly attributing the borrowed JudgeDecoding results and stating the practical limitation for verbatim reproduction. Expanded related work and a code link also improve documentation. These are useful, limited gains; the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
